thread.title: Dow Gains 200 Points as Boeing Leads Stocks Higher - Barron's

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Dow Gains 200 Points as Boeing Leads Stocks Higher - Barron's
text:
Stocks look set to for a higher open this morning after getting shellacked yesterday as President Donald Trump called for $1.5 trillion in infrastructure spending and earnings from Boeing (BA) and others restored some optimism to the market. ADP's private payrolls rose by 234,000.
Illustration: Getty Images S&P 500 futures have advanced 0.4%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have gained 211 points, or 0.8%. Nasdaq Composite futures have risen 0.5%.
Last night I noted that during the current rally, the S&P 500 has always rallied following two consecutive days of closing near the bottom of its daily range, and for now that looks to be the case. Of course, we still have a Fed rates decision to come at 2:00 p.m. ET today, which always has the potential to shake things up. Facebook (FB), meanwhile, will report earnings after the close, and we have payrolls data on Friday. So yes, there's a lot that could still go wrong. But that's a worry for later. "[Stocks] are rallying back after two down days as earnings and a 'good enough' SOTU is enough to allay bond fears and a sense of complacency ahead of more big earnings, data, and the Fed," writes Rhino Trading Partners' Michael Block.
And that will have to be good enough today.
Morning Movers Electronic Arts (EA) has jumped 7.5% to $127.62 after reporting a loss of 60 cents a share --one that included a tax hit of 57 cents--on revenue of $1.16 billion. Analysts had expected EA to report a loss of 23 cents a sales $1.14 billion. "We expect significant growth for the foreseeable future driven by cost discipline, digital sales growth, and evergreen franchises including Battlefield, the Star Wars games, and several sports titles," writes Wedbush analyst Michael Pachter.
Boeing (BA) has climbed 5.5% to $355.64 after reporting a profit of $3.06 a share on sales of $25.37 billion. Analysts had been expecting of $2.88 a share on sales of $24.88 billion. Boeing's gain has contributed about half of the Dow's total rise this morning .
Eli Lilly (LLY) has risen 1.2% to $87.10 after reporting a profit of $1.14 a share on sales of $6.2 billion. Analysts had been expecting earnings of $1.07 a share on sales of $5.9 billion. "While stronger revenues would have contributed $0.25 more EPS than we had forecast, higher R&D and SG&A than we had forecast took away $0.20 of that benefit," writes Credit Suisse analyst Vamil Divan.
Juniper Networks (JNPR) has tumbled 11% to $25.34 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings of 53 cents a share on sales of $1.24 billion, and predicting first-quarter earnings of 22 cents to 28 cents a share with sales coming in between of $1.02 billion to $1.08 billion. Analysts had predicted a fourth-quarter profit of 52 cents a share on sales of $1.24 billion, and a first quarter profit of 30 cents a share on revenue of $1.16 billion. "The case for investing in Juniper has taken a turn for the worse," writes MKM analyst Michael Genovese. "Management is not targeting y/y revenue growth again until late 2018."
Align Technology (ALGN) has fallen 3% to $262 despite reporting an adjusted profit of $1.19 a share, beating forecasts for 96 cents a share, on sales of $421.3 million, topping analyst expectations for $396 million. Align also said it expects earnings of 94 cents to 98 cents a share in the first quarter, above the Street consensus for 88 cents a share. Plans to boost spending seem to be the culprit in the stocks weakness, as Align said it doesn't expect its profit margins to increase. "We'd note the company started off last year with a similar tone and ambitious op-ex plans that were expected to limit margin expansion in 2017," writes Leerink analyst Richard Newitter. Shares of Align returned 131% in 2017.
Broadcom (AVGO) has soared has 6.5% to $256.55 after it said it expects to report a profit of $5.10 a share , above forecasts for $4.95 a share, on sales of $5.3 billion to $5.35 billion. Analyst had been predicting sales of $5.3 billion.
Foot Locker (FL) has gained 2.6% to $51.21 after getting upgraded to Outperform from Perform at Oppenheimer.
Apple Apple's (AAPL) set to report earnings tomorrow--and it's not looking good (see the View From Silicon Valley below). But Apple has one thing going for it--its one year chart:
As you can see, Apple's sitting right on its trend line, a trend line that acted as support yesterday. Apple's the biggest stock in the S&P 500, so if it drops, there's a good chance the market will drop with it .
Let's hope it holds.
The View From Silicon Valley Apple was hit with a double whammy Tuesday: After a Deutsche Bank analyst said the much-ballyhooed iPhone X is “not living up to expectations,” a report surfaced that the U.S. Justice Department and Securities and Exchange Commission are looking into Apple’s handling of older iPhones.
First, a Bloomberg report said the Feds are in the early stages of investigating whether Apple violated securities laws when it recently disclosed a software update released in early 2017 that slowed the performance of older iPhone models. The company has since apologized and vowed to release another update to resolve the issue.
U.S. investigators are wondering if Apple misled investors about the performance of older iPhones, which also aggravated consumers, Bloomberg reports. Apple had no comment.
That may be the lesser of Apple’s immediate concerns.
Deutsche Bank’s Sherri Scribner joined a chorus of analysts who are increasingly skeptical about the iPhone X’s “super cycle” that was to propel Apple through fiscal year 2018. She contends “weaker-than-expected demand” for the $1,000 iPhone X, iPhone 8 and iPhone 8 Plus, which bodes ill for Apple’s earnings guidance on Thursday. Apple reports fiscal 2018 first-quarter results after markets close that day.
Owners of older models such as iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 Plus, introduced in September 2014, were expected to trade up to the new models introduced in September 2017. But they either scoffed at the price of iPhone X, decided to hold onto their older iPhones or ditch Apple altogether for an inexpensive alternative. (I can vouch for sticking with my iPhone 6, which has performed remarkably well.)
Then there’s the rumor that has some investors really spooked: Influential Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo’s prediction that iPhone X may be discontinued as early as the summer, creating a gaping hole in the company’s flagship product line.
Don’t cry for Apple just yet, however. Wall Street analysts forecast it will rack up $87.06 billion in revenue and earnings per share of $3.83, according to 29 estimates averaged by Yahoo Finance. -- Jon Swartz
